threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think the Clissold Park café is a secret gem, not just the usual Saturday brunch spot packed with strollers.
Last night on the 196, a guy sang 'Wonderwall' karaoke-style, and a group of kids joined in. Bus driver just rolled his eyes and kept driving.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I spotted a wild rabbit munching on a discarded döner kebab under the U-Bahn station. Only in Neukölln, right?

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg do you stumble upon a kebab shop that opens at 3 AM and serves vegan döner alongside your late-night currywurst fix.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by how they know the shortcut past the construction on Valencia; tourists just wait in line at the detour.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy serenading the bus passengers at Civic Center, full-on opera. Muni folks didn’t miss a beat—clapped as the bus pulled away.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about Gaudí, but the real treasures are the hidden plazas where locals sip vermut and chat, away from the crowds.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell they're new by the way they still use Google Maps to navigate the short streets of Gràcia, looking up at the buildings like they're on a treasure hunt.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You ask for directions to the nearest tube and someone looks at you like you’ve grown a second head—Dalston doesn’t do that kind of travel.
Last night on the 37, a guy was singing loudly about his cat. Everyone just nodded along. Only in Peckham could you get a concert and a late bus.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I heard someone serenading their cat from the window while the kebab shop down the street blasted techno at 3 AM.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg do you find outdoor movie screenings in empty swimming pools during summer. It's a vibe that feels uniquely Berlin.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by their indifference to the BART breakdowns; tourists are the ones looking at their phones in panic when the trains don’t come.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Just saw a Muni driver giving directions to a lost tourist. It’s those small moments that make the city feel alive, even at rush hour.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all locals sip café amb llet in fancy places, but most of us grab a quick cortado at the corner bar. It's all about speed.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell when they walk too slowly—stopping to gawk at each Gaudí building like it's the first time they've seen a city.
